rationale: No evidence-supported optimization has all preconditions met for this workflow. P-LIT-FAIL-FAST (fail-fast: true) has synthetic passed scenarios, but the matrix spans OS × Julia-version combinations where each result is a distinct required check; required_checks are unverified and the contraindications (every matrix outcome required, full failure diagnostics required) apply, so cancelling remaining matrix jobs would reduce diagnostic coverage. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT/P-LIT-HISTORY-TIMEOUT require representative successful-duration history, but ci_history shows no completed runs and no measured baseline, so no informed timeout bound can be set and valid slow Windows/macOS Julia builds risk false timeouts. P-LIT-GHA-CACHE is not clearly additive because an artifact cache for ~/.julia/artifacts keyed on Project.toml already exists, and its benefit is observational/modest with mutable-cache contraindications. Preserving existing build/test coverage, the workflow is left unchanged.
